newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a surprise turnaround aimed at preventing Prime Minister John Howard making further concessions to Aboriginal negotiators, the Federal National Party has announced it will accept Howard's 10-point plan to resolve to contentious Wik native title conflic. Although the move reduces the likelihood the Coalition will split over Wik, there is still a significant gulf between the new position of the National Party and the farmers and that of Aborigines. Page 1.

In a move which comes as the Australian Taxation Office hardens its efforts in response to the significant threat to Government revenue posed by tax avoidance, Tax Commissioner Michael Carmody yesterday signalled a new phase in the fight against "aggressie tax planning", including options such as court action. The wealthy are expected to be hit hard by the move, with Carmody saying a number of people are paying very little tax given their wealth. Page 3.

According to the Benefits of National Road Transport Regulatory Reforms report, released by the National Road Transport Commission last Friday, Commonwealth and State reforms to Australia's road transport industry should deliver A$1 billion in yearly economic benefits and lead to lower freight rates. Page 3.

In a forecast yesterday which indicated most analysts now feel the Federal Government's 1.5 per cent jobs growth target is unattainable, a private-sector forecast by Access Economics found employment growth in 1996-97 could be as low as 1.2 per cent. The report also found unemployment could fall to 7.4 per cent by the middle of next year, but rise back to 8 per cent after that. Page 3
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Clerk of the Senate, Harry Evans, and Attorney-General's Department chief general counsel Henry Burmester have clashed over whether controversial Independent Senator Mal Colston should face a Senate inquiry along with a police investigation into his aleged travel rorts. Evans is calling for an inquiry into whether Colston lied to Parliament, while Burmester has warned that such an action could hinder the police investigation. Page 1.

In a surprise move aimed at reforming New South Wales' unreliable train services that have plagued commuters since new timetables were introduced late last year, former ABC boss David Hill was yesterday appointed as chief executive of the State Rail Authoity for a period of six months. Page 1.

After Brian Quinn was found guilty on Saturday of conspiring to defraud Coles and Coles Myer, Australian Securities Commission chairman Alan Cameron said yesterday Quinn was an example of the excesses of the 1980s when chief executives had treated public corporations like they were their own. However former Australian Stock Exchange director Raymond Schoer said although Quinn was fuelled by greed, he did not deserve to be put in the same class as Alan Bond or Christopher Skase. Page 1. --

Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge is due to release the Kasap report into Australia's palliative care program today. The report, commissioned by the Australian Health Ministers Advisory Committee, is expected to identify serious gaps in healthcare services for the dying, including a shortage of doctors with expertise in palliative care and a lack of services in rural areas. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

According to an independent report by Sydney firm Environmental Impact Reports, the city's new aircraft flight plan will spare harbourside areas, but will create a noise "hot spot" north-west of the airport in areas such as Ashfield, Burwood, Strathfield and Concord. The report, commissioned by the Herald, shows that 32 out of 40 council areas within 40 kilometres of the airport will be affected in some way by noise. Page 1.

Herb Elliott, Australia's greatest miler and winner of the 1,500 metres gold track medal at the 1960 Rome Olympics, is to return from the United States before September to take up a four-year position as director of athlete and corporate relations with th Australian Olympic Committee. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard has agreed to be the patron of a new fund to be set up for child victims of violent crime. The Alannah and Madeline Foundation - named after two girls who were killed in the Port Arthur massacre - will be launched in Melbourne on April 30 - two days after the first anniversary of their deaths. Page 1.

The Herald has learned that Lithgow Police Association branch president and local officer, Sergeant Martin Ticehurst, warned over a year before the killing of Lithgow teenager Alison Lewis last month that cuts in police numbers at night would hinder polic reaction times to major crimes. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Government's Budget Cabinet will consider a proposal tomorrow designed to save Radio Australia, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's overseas radio network, from being scrapped. With time running out to save the A$13.5 million service, the Foreign Affairs Department has been asked to pay half of the network's maintenance costs. Page 1.

Former Coles Myer chief Brian Quinn's lawyers said he was stoic last night as he faced his second night in jail. The lawyers expressed concern over Quinn's safety amongst his fellow inmates due to his supposed wealth, and arrangements are being made for is safety by authorities at the Melbourne Remand Centre before being sentenced this week. Page 1.

It has been found that children in Victorian babies' homes during the 1950s and 60s wore their pyjama tops backward so they could be pinned into their beds at night. Last week The Age revealed that thousands of children were unnecessarily placed in State care during this period, and were exposed to physical and psychological abuse. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
